title: QUIC Connectionmigration Source-Address Blocker Architecture
purpose: Describe the connectionmigration source-address proof lane that keeps local proof, hosted corroboration, and preferred-address setup boundaries explicit.
design_summary: The connectionmigration lane keeps the preferred migration address reachable with preferred_lft 0 while preserving original-path first-flight source selection. Local clean-runner proof now shows the original address first flight and later preferred-address path use, while hosted corroboration remains advisory until refreshed. This architecture keeps that evidence boundary distinct rather than widening the runtime transport contract.
alternatives_considered: Claim hosted readiness from the local clean-runner proof. Rejected because the hosted proof lane still needs a fresh artifact run.
Fold the blocker back into the generic connectionmigration proof lane. Rejected because the source-address issue deserves its own explicit advisory boundary.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Keep the preferred migration address reachable without making it the original-path first-flight source.
Do not claim server-side path promotion or rebind support.
Keep the lane advisory and outside ordinary gates.
Keep the blocker separate from the peer-characterization matrix work.
data_and_state_considerations: The source-address proof is evidenced by the preserved hosted failure notes, the current setup script, and the local clean-runner artifact bundle. The repo-owned runner shim supplies analyzer compatibility so no persistent upstream runner checkout mutation is required.
risks: Readers may overread the blocker lane as a runtime fix if the advisory boundary is not kept explicit.
The source-address issue could get conflated with broader connectionmigration support if the proof lane is not kept distinct.

supplemental_sections.heading: Scope
supplemental_sections.content: This design formalizes local source-address proof and hosted-corroboration boundaries. It does not claim hosted success, `rebind-port`, or `rebind-addr` support.
